boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the sole frozen record in the Tullahoma or Middle Tennessee Campaign [June 1863]: Hoover's Gap, June 24–26, 1863. The live NPS page gives Liberty Gap as another name, but Cist treats Liberty Gap as a separate action of McCook's corps; its losses are not added here. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the XIV Army Corps and Bate's and Johnson's brigades with Butler's Kentucky cavalry, without counts; the live field reads zero. Cist gives Bragg's effective total present on June 20 as 43,089 for the whole army. Bate says less than 700 men, about half his brigade, fought on June 24, later giving 650 engaged, against what he calls vastly superior force.
claims.rationale: Army-wide, brigade and engaged figures differ in scope; none is adopted as matched opening strength. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Cist describes Hoover's Gap as a narrow passage three miles long between high hills, followed by Matt's Hollow, a two-mile gorge, and says the gaps were held by strong Confederate forces. Bate says his artillery on an eminence commanded the exit from the gap, and that he later placed it on heights overlooking the whole battleground.
claims.rationale: Natural ground and positions chosen on the day; boundaries unset and no map verification.

claims.value: Cist says Reynolds's division led, and Wilder's brigade held the southern entrance of the gap against a two-brigade attack. Bate says he took the liberty of commanding the detachment in person, and that Stewart arrived with reinforcements about sundown and took command. NPS says Stewart told Johnson and Bate on the 26th that he was pulling back. The frozen and live commanders are Thomas and Stewart, both Major Generals.
claims.rationale: Command roles from two interested accounts and a summary; the frozen commanders do not receive automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Cist says Thomas drove the Confederates toward Fairfield on the 26th, and that Wilder's brigade then seized Matt's Hollow and on the 27th took Manchester; NPS says the Federals easily pushed aside the Kentucky cavalry holding the gap. Bate says his brigade held the Federals at bay until nightfall on the 24th and conducted the retreat of the 26th in good order.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Bragg's evacuation of Middle Tennessee is campaign context.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads Unknown; the live field reads 583 total (US 583; CS 0;). Bate says his brigade lost 146 killed and wounded of 650 engaged, nearly twenty-five per cent. Cist gives 231 killed and wounded at Liberty Gap, a separate action.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Cist's Liberty Gap figure is not assigned to Hoover's Gap; the live Confederate zero is not measured absence.

open_questions: Thomas's, Reynolds's, Wilder's, Stewart's and B. R. Johnson's reports and the returns, and whether the frozen record includes Liberty Gap, remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Cist is an interested Union staff history; Bate's report, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXIII, Part 1, is an interested Confederate brigade commander's account. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
